ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in Figure 8, the flow speed of the river water is v and is the same everywhere, and the width of the river is a. At a downstream distance b from the boat launching point A is a waterfall. In order for the small boat to cross the river safely (not fall into the waterfall), then (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: When the small boat crosses the river along the trajectory AB, the minimum speed of the boat in still water is $v_{\min}=\frac{av}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are upper and lower two horizontal lines representing the two banks of the river, and on the left a vertical double-headed arrow marks the river width as a. On the left side of the lower bank is marked the launching point A, and at a relatively right place on the upper bank is marked point B; between A and B a slanting upward dashed trajectory AB is drawn. The horizontal distance from the vertical position where A is located to the vertical dashed line below B is marked as b; to the right of B there are also multiple horizontal dashed lines, representing the downstream dangerous area or the waterfall side. From the figure it can be seen that the horizontal component of the displacement from A to B is b, and the crossing component is a. Then reason: Establish a coordinate system according to the specified method, take the water flow direction as the positive direction of the x-axis, and the crossing direction as the positive direction of the y-axis. The direction unit vector of trajectory AB is e=(b,a)/sqrt(a^2+b^2). Let the velocity of the small boat relative to the ground be along AB, with magnitude s, then the velocity relative to the ground is s e; the river water velocity is (v,0). Therefore the velocity vector of the boat in still water is u=s e-(v,0). In order to make the required still-water speed minimum, it is necessary to make |u| take a minimum with respect to s. Geometrically, this is decomposing the water flow velocity (v,0) into the AB direction and the direction perpendicular to AB; the minimum |u| equals the perpendicular component of the water flow velocity relative to the AB direction. Equivalently, at the minimum u is perpendicular to e, that is, (s e-(v,0))·e=0, so s=(v,0)·e=vb/sqrt(a^2+b^2). At this time the minimum still-water speed is v_min=sqrt(v^2-(vb/sqrt(a^2+b^2))^2)=av/sqrt(a^2+b^2).
